source.text: כִּקְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים מַ֚יִם תִּבְעֶה־אֵ֔שׁ לְהוֹדִ֥יעַ שִׁמְךָ֖ לְצָרֶ֑יךָ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ גּוֹיִ֥ם יִרְגָּֽזוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: As fire kindles brushwood, fire makes water boil, to make known your name to your foes; from before you nations will tremble.

en.L: As fire kindles brushwood, [as] fire makes water boil, to make known {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foes; from before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} nations will tremble.
en.B: Come down like fire that sets dry brush alight, like fire that brings water to the boil; make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name known to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foes, and let the nations tremble before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Come down like a fire that burns up dry sticks and makes water boil. Show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are, and make the nations shake with fear in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: Hebrew verse numbers: this is 64:1 in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text chapter 63 ends with the plea "Oh that you would tear open the heavens and come down" (63:19b), which Bibles following the older Latin and Greek division print as 64:1. So 64:1-11 here are 64:2-12 there. Isaiah is cited by the Hebrew numbers throughout.

decisions.choice: as fire ...: the wish of 63:19b goes on; God is asked to come down as fire comes on what it burns
alternatives: a new comparison standing on its own
decisions.reason: The verse has no main verb of its own. It completes the plea that God would tear open the heavens and come down (63:19b): let him come as fire, so that his name is known and the nations tremble.

decisions.choice: fire and trembling: God's coming at Sinai
decisions.reason: When the LORD came down on Mount Sinai, the mountain smoked with fire and quaked (Exodus 19:18). The prayer asks for that kind of coming again, now so that his enemies learn who he is (Exodus 9:16; Psalm 68:9).

decisions.choice: brushwood: dry twigs and brush that catch fire at once
decisions.reason: The word is rare; it names the small dry growth that burns quickly, the picture of something that cannot stand before fire.

decisions.choice: Come down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the plea of 63:19b so that the verse reads as a full sentence. Literal keeps the bare comparison.

decisions.choice: Show your enemies who you are
decisions.reason: To make a name known is to show who someone is and what he can do. Readable says that plainly.

source.text: בַּעֲשׂוֹתְךָ֥ נוֹרָא֖וֹת לֹ֣א נְקַוֶּ֑ה יָרַ֕דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you did awesome [deeds] [that] we did not wait for, you came down; from before you mountains quaked.

en.L: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did awesome [deeds] [that] we were not waiting for, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came down; from before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mountains quaked.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did fearsome things beyond all we had hoped, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came down, and the mountains shook before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did amazing and fearsome things that we never expected, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came down, and the mountains shook in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: when you did ... you came down: God's past acts are recalled
alternatives: when you do awesome things, may you come down
decisions.reason: The verbs are past. The people remember what God once did, above all at the exodus and Sinai, as the ground for asking him to do it again. Some read the verse as part of the wish ("when you do ..., may you come down").

decisions.choice: you came down; mountains quaked before you: the words of 63:19b repeated
decisions.reason: The prayer takes up its own plea from 63:19b and turns it into memory. Mountains trembling when God comes is the language of Sinai and of the old songs (Exodus 19:18; Judges 5:5; Psalm 68:9).

decisions.choice: awesome deeds: acts of God that make people afraid and amazed
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's acts at the exodus (Deuteronomy 10:21; 2 Samuel 7:23).

source.text: וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם לֹא־שָׁמְע֖וּ לֹ֣א הֶאֱזִ֑ינוּ עַ֣יִן לֹֽא־רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לִמְחַכֵּה־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And from long ago they have not heard, they have not given ear; an eye has not seen a God besides you [who] acts for [one who] waits for him.

en.L: And from of old [people] have not heard, they have not listened; an eye has not seen a God besides {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [who] acts for [the one who] waits for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Never since time began has anyone heard of it or taken it in; no eye has ever seen a God other than {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one who works for those who wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Since the world began, no one has ever heard of any God except {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and no one has ever seen one. Only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} act to help people who wait for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: no eye has seen a God besides you: the LORD alone acts for his people
decisions.reason: No one has ever known another God who works on behalf of those who trust him. The LORD's uniqueness is a theme of the whole book (43:10-11; 44:6; 45:21).

decisions.choice: quoted in 1 Corinthians 2:9
decisions.reason: Paul draws on this verse (with words like those of 52:15 and 65:16-17) for "what no eye has seen, nor ear heard ... what God has prepared for those who love him". He applies it to what God has now made known through his Spirit.

decisions.choice: waits for: hopes in God and trusts him to act
decisions.reason: The verb is used of waiting with expectation for God (30:18; Habakkuk 2:3; Daniel 12:12).

decisions.choice: people who wait for you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from speaking to God ("besides you") to speaking about him ("waits for him"). Readable keeps speaking to God so the sentence stays clear.

source.text: פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת־שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ הֵן־אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א בָּהֶ֥ם עוֹלָ֖ם וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: You meet [one who] rejoices and does righteousness, in your ways they remember you; look, you were angry and we sinned; in them long [time], and will we be saved?

en.L: You meet [the one who] rejoices and does righteousness, [those who] remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways. Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were angry, and we sinned; in them [we have been] a long [time], and will we be saved?
en.B: You go out to meet the one who delights in doing righteousness, those who keep {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in mind as they walk in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were angry, and we sinned. We have stayed in our sins so long; can we be saved?
en.R: You welcome people who are glad to do what is right and who remember how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want them to live. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} became angry, and we kept on sinning. We have been sinning for a long time. How can we ever be saved?

decisions.choice: righteousness: what is right, right conduct
decisions.reason: Here the word is the right way of living that God welcomes, not a status before God.

decisions.choice: in them a long time, and will we be saved?: we have stayed in our sins so long; can we still be saved?
alternatives: in your ways is lasting life, and we will be saved
decisions.reason: The line is short and hard. "In them" is read as the sins just named, "a long time" as how long the people have stayed in them, and the last words as a question of near despair. Others read "in your ways [is] lasting life, and we will be saved", taking "them" as God's ways. The Septuagint reads differently again ("therefore we went astray").

decisions.choice: you were angry, and we sinned: anger and sin are set side by side
decisions.reason: The two clauses are simply joined. God's anger answered the people's sin, and under that anger they went on sinning (verse 6).

decisions.choice: in our sins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "them" refers to, following the reading in m2.

decisions.choice: do what is right; remember how you want them to live
decisions.reason: Readable says "what is right" for righteousness as right conduct (m1), and explains "remember you in your ways" as keeping to the way God wants people to live.

source.text: וַנְּהִ֤י כַטָּמֵא֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וּכְבֶ֥גֶד עִדִּ֖ים כָּל־צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ וַנָּ֤בֶל כֶּֽעָלֶה֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וַעֲוֺנֵ֖נוּ כָּר֥וּחַ יִשָּׂאֻֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we have become like the unclean [one], all of us, and like a garment of menstruations [are] all our righteousnesses, and we have withered like the leaf, all of us, and our iniquities like the wind carry us away.

en.L: And we have become like the unclean [one], all of us, and like a menstrual garment [are] all our righteous deeds; and we have withered like the leaf, all of us, and our iniquities, like the wind, carry us away.
en.B: We have all turned into something unclean; our righteous deeds, every one, are like a cloth soiled by a woman's monthly blood. We fade like leaves, all of us, and our guilt carries us off like the wind.
en.R: All of us have become unclean. Even all the righteous things we do are like a cloth stained with a woman's monthly blood. We all dry up like dead leaves, and our sins blow us away like the wind.

decisions.choice: a garment of menstruation: a cloth stained by a woman's monthly flow, which made it ritually unclean
decisions.reason: Under the law a woman's monthly flow made her, and what she lay or sat on, ritually unclean for a time (Leviticus 15:19-24). This was not a sin, and the picture does not shame women. It says that even the people's best deeds carry impurity and cannot bring them near to God. The phrase is often rendered "filthy rags", which hides the image.

decisions.choice: the unclean: someone ritually unclean, who must keep away from the holy
decisions.reason: The word is used of the person with a skin disease who must cry out "Unclean, unclean!" (Leviticus 13:45; compare 6:5; 52:1). The whole people now stand where that person stood.

decisions.choice: our righteousnesses: our righteous deeds
decisions.reason: The plural means acts of righteousness, the good things the people do (compare 33:15; Ezekiel 3:20).

decisions.choice: withered like a leaf, carried off by the wind: life fading and swept away
decisions.reason: A dry leaf falls and is blown away (1:30; 40:7-8; Psalm 1:4). Their sins are the wind that drives them off.

decisions.choice: a cloth soiled (stained) by a woman's monthly blood
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the cloth plainly. Balanced and Readable say what it is in respectful, everyday words rather than a euphemism.

source.text: וְאֵין־קוֹרֵ֣א בְשִׁמְךָ֔ מִתְעוֹרֵ֖ר לְהַחֲזִ֣יק בָּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־הִסְתַּ֤רְתָּ פָנֶ֨יךָ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וַתְּמוּגֵ֖נוּ בְּיַד־עֲוֺנֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And there [is] no one calling on your name, rousing himself to take hold of you, for you have hidden your face from us and you have melted us in the hand of our iniquity.

en.L: And there [is] no one who calls on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, who rouses himself to take hold of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have hidden {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from us and have melted us in the hand of our iniquity.
en.B: Not one of us calls on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; no one stirs to hold on to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have hidden {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from us and let us melt away in the grip of our guilt.
en.R: Nobody prays to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and nobody makes an effort to hold on to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. That is because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from us. You have let our sins destroy us.

decisions.choice: you have hidden your face: God has withdrawn his favor and presence
decisions.reason: To hide the face is to turn away and give no help (8:17; 54:8; Deuteronomy 31:17-18).

decisions.choice: you have melted us in the hand of our iniquity: the Hebrew text is followed
alternatives: you have handed us over to our iniquity
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says God has let the people melt away in the power of their sin. The Septuagint has "you have handed us over" because of our sins, which matches a Hebrew word that differs by little; some follow it. The Hebrew makes good sense and is kept.

decisions.choice: in the hand of: in the power of
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (Genesis 9:2; Judges 2:14). Their own guilt holds them.

decisions.choice: prays to you; turned away from us
decisions.reason: Readable explains "calls on your name" as praying and "hidden your face" as turning away.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אָבִ֣ינוּ אָ֑תָּה אֲנַ֤חְנוּ הַחֹ֨מֶר֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה יֹצְרֵ֔נוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדְךָ֖ כֻּלָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, Yahweh, our father [are] you; we [are] the clay, and you [are] our former, and the work of your hand [are] we all.

en.L: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] our Father; we [are] the clay, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] our potter, and the work of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand [are] we all.
en.B: But now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are our Father. We are the clay, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the potter who shaped us; every one of us is what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand has made.
en.R: But {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are our Father. We are like clay, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are like a potter who shapes the clay. You made every one of us with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands.

decisions.choice: you are our Father: God who made his people and cares for them as his own
decisions.reason: The prayer already called on God as Father in 63:16. He is Father as the one who brought Israel into being and owns it (Deuteronomy 32:6; Malachi 2:10).

decisions.choice: we are the clay, you our potter: we belong to the one who formed us
decisions.reason: The verb "form" is the potter's word, used when God forms the man from dust (Genesis 2:7). Isaiah uses the picture elsewhere to rebuke those who argue with their maker (29:16; 45:9); here it is a plea: you made us, so do not abandon your work (Jeremiah 18:1-6; Romans 9:20-21).

decisions.choice: like clay; like a potter who shapes the clay
decisions.reason: Readable marks the picture as a comparison so a young reader follows it.

source.text: אַל־תִּקְצֹ֤ף יְהוָה֙ עַד־מְאֹ֔ד וְאַל־לָעַ֖ד תִּזְכֹּ֣ר עָוֺ֑ן הֵ֥ן הַבֶּט־נָ֖א עַמְּךָ֥ כֻלָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be angry, Yahweh, to muchness, and do not forever remember iniquity; look, please, your people [are] we all.

en.L: Do not be angry, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to the utmost, and do not remember iniquity forever. Look, please: {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people [are] we all.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger go too far, and do not keep our guilt in mind forever. Look at us, we beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}: all of us are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please do not stay so angry with us. Do not remember our sins forever. Please look at us. We are all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

decisions.choice: remember iniquity: hold sin against someone and punish it
decisions.reason: For God to remember sin is to act on it; to forget it is to forgive (43:25; Psalm 79:8; Jeremiah 31:34).

decisions.choice: to muchness: to the utmost, beyond measure
decisions.reason: The same words close the prayer in verse 11, so the plea that God's anger not go too far frames the end of it.

decisions.choice: we are all your people: an appeal to God's covenant
decisions.reason: The people base their plea not on their deeds (verse 5) but on belonging to God (63:19; Exodus 33:13).

decisions.choice: our guilt; our sins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose iniquity is meant, as the prayer's context makes plain.

source.text: עָרֵ֥י קָדְשְׁךָ֖ הָי֣וּ מִדְבָּ֑ר צִיּוֹן֙ מִדְבָּ֣ר הָיָ֔תָה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שְׁמָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The cities of your holiness have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.

en.L: The cities of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holiness have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
en.B: Your holy cities have turned into open wilderness. Zion is now a wilderness; Jerusalem lies desolate.
en.R: Your holy cities have become like a desert. Zion is a desert, and Jerusalem is empty and ruined.

decisions.choice: your holy cities: the towns of Judah, the land that belongs to God
decisions.reason: The land is God's holy land, so its towns are his (Zechariah 2:16; Psalm 78:54).

decisions.choice: wilderness, desolation: Jerusalem lies ruined and empty
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks as if Jerusalem and the temple already lie in ruins, as they did after the Babylonians destroyed the city in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:8-10). A wilderness is land without settled people, not only sand.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for empty land where no one lives.

source.text: בֵּ֧ית קָדְשֵׁ֣נוּ וְתִפְאַרְתֵּ֗נוּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִֽלְל֨וּךָ֙ אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ הָיָ֖ה לִשְׂרֵ֣פַת אֵ֑שׁ וְכָל־מַחֲמַדֵּ֖ינוּ הָיָ֥ה לְחָרְבָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The house of our holiness and our splendor, where our fathers praised you, has become a burning of fire, and all our desirable things have become a ruin.

en.L: The house of our holiness and our splendor, where our fathers praised {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, has become [something] burned by fire, and all our precious [things] have become a ruin.
en.B: Our holy and splendid house, where our ancestors once praised {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, has been given to the fire, and every precious thing we had is now rubble.
en.R: The holy temple we were so proud of, where our ancestors praised {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, has burned down. All the things we loved are ruined.

decisions.choice: the house of our holiness: the temple in Jerusalem, burned with fire
decisions.reason: The Babylonians burned the house of the LORD in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9; Psalm 74:7). It was the people's holy place and their pride.

decisions.choice: our desirable things: our treasures, everything we prized
decisions.reason: The word is used of precious things lost when Jerusalem fell (Lamentations 1:10-11; 2:4). It may mean the temple's treasures or all the city's pleasant places.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Readable names the house the prayer means.

source.text: הַעַל־אֵ֥לֶּה תִתְאַפַּ֖ק יְהוָ֑ה תֶּחֱשֶׁ֥ה וּתְעַנֵּ֖נוּ עַד־מְאֹֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Over these [things] will you restrain yourself, Yahweh? Will you be silent and afflict us to muchness?

en.L: Over these [things] will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} back, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be silent and afflict us to the utmost?
en.B: With all this before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} still hold {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} back? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep silent and afflict us so severely?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, after seeing all this, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} still do nothing? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stay silent and keep making us suffer so much?

decisions.choice: will you hold back ... will you be silent: the prayer ends with questions
decisions.reason: The prayer that began at 63:7 ends without an answer of its own. The LORD replies in chapter 65: "I will not keep silent" (65:6).

decisions.choice: restrain yourself: hold back from acting
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when God says he has long held himself back (42:14) and when the prayer asks where his compassion has gone (63:15).

decisions.choice: still do nothing; keep making us suffer
decisions.reason: Readable says what holding back means here (not acting to help) and puts "afflict" in plain words.
